notes: Fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c, head 3e3581d, skill_hash 03a6bb2b...): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0, a model_id matching the requested model, and reads of SKILL.md and library-design.md; each transcript shows Read calls on both files before the Write of weather.ex.

git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes SKILL.md (the When to load and Reviewing code bullets, a defstruct sentence in Update structs, the new Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, two new sentences in the do: rule, the new directive-order rule, step 4 of Before you finish), the ETS example in processes.md, and testing.md. None of the nine rules in the case's list changed (Return/raise, Group related parameters, one return shape and Read configuration at runtime in SKILL.md; the five library-design.md rules, a file the diff does not touch), so all nine were graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/library-client-skill.json: Make polymorphism explicit is met when the API key taken from opts, and the other option values, reach a guard before the request (or the key is a guarded positional argument), and Add specs exempts @impl callbacks.

All nine case rules are clean in all five runs. Every run checks the API key's type before it reaches the header: opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 in a guarded private function after Keyword.validate!/2 (opus-1 build/4 line 95, haiku-1 build/3 line 62, haiku-2 validate!/1 line 67), sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 as a guarded positional argument of new/2 (lines 118 and 50). haiku-1 and haiku-2 have no bang variant. sonnet-2 hides the key with @derive {Inspect, only: [:base_url]}, the key living only in its :req field; the other four derive except: [:api_key].

Changed rule outside the list, applied to other_violations under its current text: Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. The sentences that decide it: "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper. The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line." Violating runs: 1 of 5, haiku-2 (api_error/2, lines 90-91 and 93-94; its validate!/1 at lines 66-68 is the kept guard wrap). The b sweep's opus-1 violation does not recur: this opus-1 writes every Error.message/1 clause as a block. haiku-1's handle_response/1 keeps two short clauses on do: beside two blocks, one of which only has a guard wrap, so most clauses do not need blocks; set apart with blank lines, it is clean. No file has an if with do:.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call (new since 0397dec), graded on "When an argument is a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines, build it first under a name that says what it is, write it one field per line, and set each multi-line statement apart with a blank line." The rule's own write example binds a call whose keyword options span several lines to a name (formatter = Logger.Formatter.new(format: ..., metadata: ..., colors: ...)), so that shape is not counted: opts = Keyword.validate!(opts, [...]) across several lines (opus-1 lines 54-60, sonnet-1 lines 119-124, sonnet-2 lines 51-56), request = Req.new(...) (haiku-1 lines 67-72) and req = Req.new(...) (sonnet-2 lines 101-106). haiku-2 lines 71-75 write Req.new(...) as the whole body of build_request/1, whose result line 57 names request; counted the same way, a borderline call. Every other multi-line literal is built under a name first (opus-1 request_options line 75 and base_options lines 131-135, sonnet-1 options lines 176-180, sonnet-2 forecast lines 143-147) or is a return value. Result: 0 of 5. Counting the multi-line Keyword.validate!/2 defaults lists would make opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 violate.

The other changed rules outside the list were not broken: every nil-default defstruct field is a bare atom (keyword entries are real defaults: haiku-2 line 21 base_url: @default_base_url, sonnet-1 line 90 req_options: []); each module opens with alias only; no run has tests for Before you finish step 4.

Unchanged rules outside the list, judged as in the b sweep: sonnet-1 writes a one-step with (line 144), which Chain fallible steps with `with` forbids. Match every expected shape is flagged for sonnet-2, whose Error doc defines :api_error as a 4xx/5xx status while every non-2xx response lands there (a 302 through a stub Req returns reason: :api_error, status: 302), as the b sweep flagged its sonnet runs; sonnet-1 now documents :api as a non-2xx status (line 7), opus-1 documents its catch-all as a body the client does not understand, and haiku-1 and haiku-2 define no reason kinds for the docs to contradict. sonnet-2's fetch_forecast/3 returns {:error, %Error{}} but is an HTTP fetch, not the key lookup the naming bullet describes, so it is not counted.

Before you finish is flagged only where the file fails mix format --check-formatted, as in the previous sweeps: all five pass (rechecked in the scratch folder). opus-1 and sonnet-1 ran mix format; haiku-1's one elixir syntax check was refused by the permission prompt; haiku-2 and sonnet-2 ran no shell command. No session compiled its file.

Not graded, as in the previous sweeps, but noted in the summaries and matching result.json compiles: sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile, and against a stub Req a non-binary API key fails with FunctionClauseError in WeatherClient.new/2 in both. opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 do not compile, independently of Req, because WeatherClient builds %WeatherClient.Error{} (and in the Haiku runs %WeatherClient.Forecast{}) before the file defines that module.
